title: Flexibility for Workers Education Act
official_title: To amend the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 to exclude certain activities from hours worked, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Failed in the House on January 13, 2026 by a 209-215 vote. A failed floor vote ends the bill’s progress in this Congress.
summary: Says that time employees spend in voluntary, off-hours education or training does not count as paid 'hours worked' under federal wage law.
brief: Amends the Fair Labor Standards Act so voluntary, off-the-clock education or training time is not counted as hours worked.

top_lines.headline: Off-Hours Training Not Paid Time
subs: Voluntary off-hours education or training excluded from 'hours worked'
Applies whether or not the employer offers the activity
Activity must be voluntary, with no productive work performed

items.main: Names the Act the “Flexibility for Workers Education Act”.
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Treatment of Attendance or Participation in Certain Activities

items.main: Excludes voluntary, off-hours education or training time from 'hours worked' under the Fair Labor Standards Act.
items.detail: Rewrites FLSA Section 3(o) (29 U.S.C. 203(o)). For minimum-wage and overtime purposes, time spent attending lectures, education or training programs, and similar activities is excluded from hours worked if it occurs outside regular working hours, is voluntary (with no adverse effect on employment for not attending), and involves no productive work for the employer. The existing exclusion for clothes-changing and washing under a collective-bargaining agreement is retained. The change applies to hours worked on or after enactment.

gaps: The exclusion depends on attendance being 'voluntary' and not affecting employment, but the bill does not specify how a worker disputes an employer's claim that training was voluntary.
It excludes the time from 'hours worked' for federal wage purposes but does not address state wage-and-hour laws.

featured_quotes.name: Mrs. Hinson
featured_quotes.text: For too long, we know that Washington, D.C., has pursued policies that left American workers behind. Republicans continue to advance progrowth, proworker policies that expand opportunity, reward hard work, and help Americans to get ahead. No matter where I go out in Iowa--Main Street businesses, farm shops, manufacturing facilities, healthcare facilities--I meet the hardworking men and women of Iowa who want to take that next step in their careers. They want to build skills.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Norcross
featured_quotes.text: Yes, I said that. This disastrous bill would be a blueprint to commit wage theft on a silver platter. I know what it is like to be cheated out of wages. That happened to me, unfortunately, when I was a younger man. The rules that are set up are there to protect those who had the least ability to protect themselves. A fair day's pay for a hard day's work. This is not a slogan. It is a principle of who we are in this country. It is those values that hold this country together. This bill is pushing corporations to create a loophole.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Scott
featured_quotes.text: Mr. Speaker, according to last week's Bureau of Labor statistics, 2025 was the worst year for job growth in this country since the last Trump administration. 2025 had 3 months of job losses. Meanwhile, President Biden had 48 consecutive months without a single loss. At this point in President Biden's term, he had already created millions of jobs. At the end of the first year, President Trump has only created a few hundred thousand.

modified: FLSA 'hours worked' (Section 3(o), 29 U.S.C. 203(o)) now also excludes voluntary off-hours education and training time
Excluded-activity language narrowed/reworded from "lectures, education or training programs, and similar activities" to "an education or training program or a similar activity (such as a lecture)"

Voluntariness condition (B) rewritten: instead of requiring that continued employment and working conditions "not adversely affected," the employer simply may not "take adverse action against the employee" for non-attendance
Condition (C) broadened from barring "any productive work" to barring "any work" for the employer during attendance
